chapter: Bands, leaders and radio of the thirties and forties
title: The Swing Six and the 1937 NBC audition band
summary: Kline lists the Swing Six personnel and Hutto discusses the November 1937 NBC audition record and his forgotten theme song for a sustaining orchestra.

bands.name: Chauncey Morehouse and the Swing Six

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Then we come down to your band, Chauncey Morehouse and his Swing Six. Charlie Spivak on trumpet, George Brunies -trombone, quite a setup, Jimmy Lytell on clarinet, Claude Thornhill on piano, Artie Bernstein on string bass and you on the drums and vibes.
Yeah.
You led the group.
Yeah.
You didn't mind leading your own group.
No.
Okay. What kind of a group was it? Was it a small group? Was it jazz, dance?
It was a small jazz dance.
You played for both dances and jazz.
Yeah.
Both. Okay. Did you play for dance or just record?
I played for the jazz dance.
You did.
Yeah.
Okay.

In this period, and I don't know whether you have it in your notes or not, there is an audition record that he made for NBC in November, 1937. That was shortly after he had done the Larry Clinton record. And the personnel is not listed. And it may or may not be the same as he used for Brunswick in March. But I can provide you with a tape of that too. It's a 16 inch transcription. And he has this theme. And regrettably he composed but he doesn't know the name of the theme.
The theme song, he does not know the name.
Of the orchestra, he doesn't recall.
Don't recall the name of the theme song.
Right.
Isn't that a shame. It's one that you composed.
Do you recall the orchestra you had for NBC? I think he said NBC wanted him as a sustaining, I mean they would have times when for some reason or another....
That's right.
There was no commercial broadcast and they would just switch to a band there in New York....
That's right.
...As a sustaining orchestra And that's what he auditioned for. How, whether he got it, I don't know.
